engagement_title: Cellar & Cru autumn selection: bring two evenings of counter photography to one shelf white, recover the merchant's mark off a letterpressed card, rebuild the printer's shelf-talker into a live run, and hand the shop floor and the trade tasting one editable set
vertical: Food, Restaurant and Beverage, independent fine-wine merchant selling across the counter to retail customers and to restaurant buyers (Edinburgh, Scotland)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the recurring independent-wine-merchant brief posted on Upwork and Freelancer.com, 'shelf talkers / tasting cards, one per wine on our list', where the merchant supplies a spreadsheet of wines with region, vintage, buyer's note, score and price plus a folder of self-shot bottle photographs, and asks for printed cards that make the shelf read as one curated selection. Co-anchor: the equally common 'InDesign data merge from our printer's PDF' brief, where the client no longer holds a working file and supplies only the flat press PDF the printer produced last season, with the standing instruction to keep the artwork exactly as it is and put this season's data through it. The ledger records this slot (LAYOUT-B-13, absorbing AO-72) as a record-per-page merge with a bottle-shot column, one_line_ask 'so the shop floor reads as one curated set', and the triage verdict is STRENGTHEN: the concept, the collateral set and the price-band logic are right, but as banked the engagement sat almost entirely on the merge surface with the photography and the merchant's own mark treated as plumbing. LAYOUT-31 keeps the concept and the deliverables and restores the commission the merchant actually posts: the bottles have to be fixed, the mark has to be recovered because the original artwork left with the designer, and the point of fixing both is that the printed cards, the bay panel and the November trade tasting all come out of one selection and have to agree. No real merchant, producer, critic or publication appears; the house, its wines and its growers are coined.
client_one_liner: Fourteen wines, two evenings of counter photography that do not match, a shelf-talker the printer built and we cannot open, and an autumn selection that goes on the shelf in three weeks.
client_brief:
Cellar & Cru, autumn selection.

We are an independent wine merchant on a side street off the main shopping run. Fourteen wines go into the autumn selection and they go on the shelf in three weeks. Every bottle on our floor carries a card in front of it: the wine, the grower, the region, the vintage, our buyer's note, the score where there is one, and the price. That card is how we sell wine when there is one of us on the floor and eleven people in the shop.

The photography is the first problem. We shoot the bottles ourselves on the counter after closing. We did most of them one evening and the rest the following week, and laid out together they do not look like one shelf. Bottles are the awkward part: dark glass on a dark counter, and the label is the whole point, because a customer recognises a wine by its label before they read a word of it.

What we need from the pictures: every bottle looking like it was shot the same evening, each one lifted onto a clean pale ground for the card, and one picture per wine that shows the whole bottle rather than the neck or the shoulder.

There is also our mark. It is on every card and on everything else we print. The artwork went with the designer who moved abroad, so what we have is a photograph of the letterpressed compliments card he had made for us. We need it back as something we can actually place.

The second problem is the cards themselves. Our printer made last year's talkers off our old list. We have the file they sent us and nothing else, and nobody here knows how it was put together. Keep it as it is, our customers know it, and put this autumn's wines, notes, scores and prices through it. Send us the press file for the printer.

Then the pieces we do not have at all. A shelf-end panel for the bay, a by-the-glass list for the tasting bench, and a short set of slides for the trade tasting we host for restaurant buyers in November. All of that back as one file we can edit ourselves, because prices move with the exchange rate and I am not commissioning this again in February.

Bottles run fourteen to two hundred and twenty pounds. Our customers are forty to sixty-five and they read labels. Restrained, no shouting. Our list is attached, and if anything in it looks wrong to you, say so before it prints.
price_band_and_audience: Bottles from 14 pounds (an entry Loire white, a co-op red) to 220 pounds (a single-vineyard northern Rhone syrah, a mature Piedmontese nebbiolo). Buyer 40 to 65, a confident domestic drinker or a restaurant buyer building a by-the-glass list, who reads a shelf card the way a reader reads a review and who treats visual noise as a signal about the wine behind it. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct artefact is restrained and led by grower, region and vintage: generous white space, one quiet type system, the score present but small, the price plain in the run of the card, the bottle photographed straight and lifted onto a calm pale ground so the label carries. Push it toward the supermarket aisle register, price set huge, a shouting discount badge, saturated bottle photography on a dark dramatic ground, and a 220 pound bottle reads as a 6 pound bottle with an inflated ticket, which is precisely the commercial failure this merchant is paying to avoid. Push it the other way into fashion-brand minimalism where the vintage and the region are hard to find and the shop loses the one thing the card is for, which is selling wine when nobody is free to talk. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,000 pounds fixed, or 40 to 65 pounds an hour across 30 to 45 hours.

brand_identity.tagline: Wine worth the walk down the side street
brand_identity.sector: An independent fine wine merchant selling across the counter to retail customers and to restaurant buyers building by the glass lists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Established 2009, on a side street off the main shopping run in Edinburgh, Scotland. A small counter operation, one or two on the floor, an owner who buys the list himself.
brand_identity.about: Cellar & Cru is a merchant, not a shop that happens to sell wine. The owner tastes and chooses every line, and the selection changes with the season. When there is one of us on the floor and eleven people in, the shelf card is how a wine sells itself, so the card carries the grower, the region, the vintage, our note, the score and the price.
brand_identity.audience: Confident domestic drinkers and restaurant buyers aged 40 to 65 who read a shelf card the way a reader reads a review, and who treat visual noise as a signal about the wine behind it.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Independent fine wine. Bottles from 14 pounds to 220. The card is restrained and led by grower, region and vintage: generous white space, the score present but small, the price plain in the run of the line. Never the supermarket aisle, never fashion brand minimalism that hides the vintage.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet oldstyle serif for wine names and running notes, set with air, paired with a plain grotesque for regions, vintages and figures. Readable at 40 to 65, restrained rather than loud or fashionable.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, measured and honest, the owner describing a wine as if standing beside you. It says what a wine is and is not, without hyperbole. Example: A co-op red that drinks well above its price, so long as you open it an hour before.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original mark artwork went with the designer who moved abroad. The only clean version we hold is a photograph of the letterpressed compliments card he had made for us, carrying the mark at about 45mm. The autumn list, buyer's notes, scores and prices arrive from the till export.
brand_identity.values: A selection chosen by one buyer with a point of view, and a shop floor that sells wine honestly even when nobody is free to talk.

assets_supplied.name: bottle_shots/ (16 frames, 4200 x 2800)
assets_supplied.kind: The merchant's own bottle photography, shot on the shop counter after closing on two separate evenings, available light plus a counter lamp.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Most of them one evening, the rest the week after. Same counter, same camera. Together they do not look like one shelf."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The counter lamp was moved between the evenings, so seven frames sit a full step warmer and read as a different glass colour rather than a different light, and six of the wines are in near-black Burgundy or Rhone glass photographed against the dark oak counter, so a one-call knockout finds almost no luminance difference along the shoulder and bites into it, returning a clean, plausible, well-feathered cutout whose shoulder line has been cut flat and whose capsule carries a soft halo. Sixteen frames cover fourteen wines: one wine was reshot and the duplicate is not marked, and one listed wine has no frame at all.

assets_supplied.name: talker_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of last season's shelf-talker, A6 portrait, one wine per page, fonts embedded, produced from the merchant's old list through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries the mark, a bottle image, the wine block and a score badge.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer sent us last year. We do not have the working file and nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two facts nobody at the shop could tell you. The system that produced the card set the entire body, grower, region, vintage, score, buyer's note, stockist code and price, as ONE continuous story with tab characters between each label and its value, so there are no per-field frames to map and every value must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story, and the mapping readout of that story silently omits the run holding the stockist code while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed, every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic and the two fields sitting past the omission never become placeholders at all. Separately, the buyer's note sits in a fixed-measure frame sized to last year's notes. And the card ground, named Chalk White in the palette, is a placed warm laid stock rather than a flat process fill: rendered at trim it reproduces a measurable step warmer and slightly darker than a flat #F1ECE1 fill, so a bottle lifted onto a ground matched to the nominal swatch sits in a visible cool rectangular patch on every rendered card, a mismatch that appears only where the cutout ground meets the card ground on the rendered page and only after a card has been rendered.

assets_supplied.name: autumn_list.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the shop's till and stock system, one row per line, with columns for wine, grower, region, vintage, style, buyer's note, score, score source, bottle price, case price, status and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our list, straight out of the till system. The notes and the scores are ours and the prices are current as of Monday."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Sixteen rows for fourteen sellable wines: two allocation-only lines the till still emits, flagged only by a status column the merchant never mentions. Vintages carry a leading apostrophe from the spreadsheet that exported them, the buyer's notes run from 90 to 340 characters because three were written by the owner and the rest by the part-time buyer, and the image column holds full local paths rather than bare filenames and lacks the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, so a naive run binds one bottle to every card or binds no bottles at all.

assets_supplied.name: mark_card.jpg (3600 x 2400)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the shop's letterpressed compliments card lying on the counter, carrying the merchant's mark at about 45mm wide, shot in daylight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only clean version of our mark we have left. The original artwork went with the designer."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is a monoline vine-and-key device with an enclosed counter inside the key bow and a hairline rule beneath the wordmark, pressed into soft cotton paper so the strokes sit close to the paper's own texture. A knockout cannot punch that enclosed counter and collapses on the disjoint lettering, and a trace taken from a selection reads immaculately at screen scale while carrying the paper's tooth as broken edges in the hairline.

assets_supplied.name: buyer_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A page from the owner describing the selection in plain language: which wines are the anchors of the bay, which two are the ones he wants people to try, and how he talks about the scores.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How I would describe the selection if I were standing there."

assets_supplied.name: bay_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Phone snap of the shelf bay with last season's talkers in place, supplied as a feel reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the bay. The cards sit in wooden fins in front of the bottles."

acceptance_bar: All fourteen wines read as one selection: one shelf white, one black point, one bottle scale, judged with the fourteen laid out as the bay rather than one at a time.
Every label reads as the label the customer will recognise, and no correction has pushed a label paper, a capsule or a glass colour to something the bottle is not.
Each wine has one picture showing the whole bottle and one lifted onto the agreed pale ground for the card, and the two agree with each other.
The cut edge of every bottle follows the bottle: no flattened shoulder, no clipped capsule, no halo carried in from the counter, judged on the pale card ground rather than on the dark original.

The pale ground the bottles are lifted onto agrees with the printer's card as it actually renders, not merely with the nominal Chalk White swatch: no bottle sits in a rectangular ground patch a different white to the card around it, judged on the merged card at trim rather than on the cutout in isolation.
No delivered file is larger than the frame it came from, and the note lists every picture that was resized and by how much.
The recovered mark is delivered as placeable artwork with no opaque backing box, and it holds as the mark at the size it is actually reproduced on the card, not only at the size it was inspected.

Shelf-talkers: exactly one page per sellable wine in list order, every field the 2025 card carried present on every page, every value bound verbatim from the list, and the bottle on each card the wine named on that card.

Nothing in the list may be shortened, reworded or abbreviated to make it fit. Anything that will not fit inside the card as it stands, tell us in writing before it goes to the printer, and no card may go out carrying a note that stops mid sentence.
The press file renders at real print resolution at A6 trim, and no card exists for a line the shop cannot sell.
The bay panel, the by-the-glass list and the November slides come back as one working file we can edit ourselves, each at its own size, plus the source it was built from.
In that file the words are live text, the list is a real table and the mark is real artwork, not a picture of a page.
One type system across all of it, and the note names per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
A written note: what was done to each picture and why it differs from its neighbours, anything in our list you questioned and what you did about it, and anything the card could not carry.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including the trace of the merchant's mark
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_color_temperature, image_adjust_single_color_saturation, image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.detection_confidence and metadata.tradeoffs, image_remove_background with and without backgroundColor, image_fill_area, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Fixes one shelf white from the better evening and corrects each wine toward it with its own parameter set, because a batched call applies one identical set and seven frames were shot under a moved lamp. Protects the labels, which are the thing the customer recognises. Lifts each bottle onto the agreed card ground, routing per bottle because near-black glass on a dark counter cannot be knocked out the same way as a pale Alsace flute. Recovers the merchant's mark off a photographed letterpressed card and traces it to placeable vector. Counted honestly as one surface: image_vectorize is a Photoshop-family tool and no Illustrator tool is called anywhere in this engagement. This surface is also returned to after the merge has rendered, because the ground each bottle was lifted onto can only be checked against the printer's card once a card exists, and if the cutouts patch against the stock as it actually reproduces all fourteen are re-grounded here through image_fill_area to the measured value and re-judged as a set before they are re-bound and re-merged.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge-template authoring, data merge and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and as validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: Rebuilds the printer's flat card into a live merge template with no working file to start from, reads the real frame inventory before promising any field map, reconstructs the true story text from the IDML content runs rather than trusting the mapping readout, binds each wine's own bottle into the card's graphic frame, excludes the lines the shop cannot sell by record range, and runs the selection at one record per page to a press PDF plus 300 ppi proofs rendered from the merged document rather than requested at merge time.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express, asset_search(CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The three pieces the merchant does not have: an A1 shelf-end bay panel at true physical dimensions, an A4 by-the-glass list for the tasting bench with the wines as a genuine table, and the November trade-tasting slides, authored as one HTML with roots at three canvas sizes and exported as one native editable document. The recovered mark goes in as inline vector rather than a picture, every photograph is carried as embedded image data, and prices stay live text because they move with the exchange rate.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend once per typographic role, font_styles for the numeric OpenType weights, find_fonts to launder every name, get_fontkit_embed_url for one kit consumed through the returned css_stack
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the bay panel, the bench list and the slides, and the specification of it in the handover. The pairing is the agent's own art direction because the recommender refuses to pair, and it has to land restrained and readable at 40 to 65 rather than on either a supermarket or a fashion register. The handover must also state that no face chosen here can reach the printed talker, since there is no font file download, so the card's typography stays the printer's.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, isGenTech excluded, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed vineyard or cellar frame for the A1 bay panel and the opening slide, which the merchant cannot photograph, graded into the same neutral as the bottles and judged beside them. Plus the persistent board the owner approves the selection from before the press file is committed, sent within the twelve-item placement cap and reconciled against failedItems.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The talkers are record per page against a layout the merchant has told you to keep, so they belong on the merge surface. The bay panel, bench list and slides do not exist yet, need three canvas sizes and must stay editable, so they belong on HTML authoring. Authoring the talkers from scratch throws away the card the customers know; trying to merge the bay panel discovers record per page cannot produce three canvas sizes.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the sixteen bottle frames, the 2025 talker PDF, the till export and the mark photograph, holding each presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Manifest discipline: forty artefacts later the mapping between URL and wine has to still be trustworthy.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by wine and role.

trajectory.action: Preview every frame and triage: which evening, how warm, how level, how dark the glass is against the counter, how the label sits, and whether the frames and the list actually describe the same fourteen wines.
trajectory.judgement: The merchant says same counter, same camera. Half the shoot disagrees. The agent also has to notice which bottles are close in value to the counter behind them before deciding how to lift them, and to read a sixteen-row export against fourteen frames and two lines it may not be entitled to print at all.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note covering evening, warmth, level, subject separation and identity.

trajectory.action: Level the frames that are off level.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it precedes every crop and isolation decision rather than following one.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed.

trajectory.action: Fix one shelf white from the better evening and correct each wine toward it with its own parameter set, recording what was dialled per frame.
trajectory.judgement: One destination held across fourteen frames, not fourteen locally optimised pictures. The seven warm frames need a materially different correction to arrive at the same neutral, and a single batched call would apply one identical set and ship half the bay amber.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen graded masters at source scale with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections to protect the labels: hold label paper honest without bleaching the print, keep capsule foils from going brassy, keep near-black glass off crush so the bottle still has a shoulder.
trajectory.judgement: The label is the merchant's actual commercial requirement rather than a cosmetic one. Prompt wording is the gate, and a selection named for the substrate pulls the whole bottle instead of the label, which has to be recognised as the wrong selection rather than accepted because the call succeeded.
trajectory.produces: Label-protected masters with masked parameters recorded per wine.

trajectory.action: Derive the whole-bottle picture per wine, reading the detection confidence and tradeoffs each crop returns rather than trusting success, then lay the fourteen out as the bay they are for and settle one bottle scale across the set.
trajectory.judgement: Bottle scale is a set-level decision that cannot be made one picture at a time: a Burgundy bottle and a Rhone bottle at the same frame height are not at the same scale on the shelf.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen whole-bottle pictures at a settled scale, laid out as the bay, with the crop metadata transcribed.

trajectory.action: Propose two pale grounds for the card cutouts, a warm paper and a cool near-white, and pick one against the printed card the bottles will actually land on.
trajectory.judgement: A taste decision with a defence attached, and one bound to a downstream fact: the ground has to sit with the tint of the printer's own card stock, because a bottle lifted onto the wrong white shows as a visible patch on every one of fourteen cards and is only fixable by re-isolating all fourteen.
trajectory.produces: Two proposed grounds and a written pick with the reason recorded.

trajectory.action: Lift each bottle onto the chosen ground, routing per bottle: pale and well separated bottles through the one-call knockout, dark glass against the dark counter through a selection of the bottle's own material, inverted and filled to the ground.
trajectory.judgement: The route is a per-bottle decision made by looking at the bottle rather than a policy applied to fourteen. A knockout that succeeds is not the same as a cut edge that follows the glass.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen bottles on the agreed ground with the route recorded per wine.

trajectory.action: Recover the merchant's mark from the letterpressed card: select the ink by its own visual properties rather than by the card it sits on, invert, crop to the selection's own bounds, trace it, strip the trace's full-canvas backing path and inject a viewBox, and render a high-resolution plate of the same artwork for the merge surface.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the paper and the trace returns a card-shaped blob. The enclosed counter in the key bow cannot be punched by a knockout, so the route is selection and fill rather than background removal, and the traced result has to be judged as artwork rather than accepted as output.
trajectory.produces: The mark as placeable vector with no backing box, plus a raster plate for the printed card.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the till export against the pictures and the buyer's notes, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with the image column in the form the merge contract requires and bare filenames in the cells, upload the card masters and build the image map against them.
trajectory.judgement: Real data-prep work: lines the shop cannot sell, vintages carrying a spreadsheet artefact, and an image column that does not satisfy the contract. The agent decides which of those are its call and which are the merchant's, and how to say so before anything prints.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded masters, the image map, and a first list of questions for the merchant.

trajectory.action: Convert the 2025 talker to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, and read the true frame inventory and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the printer's system happened to produce, not by what the printed card looks like. Reading the document is the only honest basis for promising a field map.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real integer ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every field on the card plus the bottle image, ordering any rows that share a uid in descending position against the original text, and pass it back through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right action for the granularity that came back, computing every offset from a source of truth the agent has chosen deliberately, and passing the whole mapping across as one stringified object with integer page-item ids.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering the card fields and the bottle frame.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the RESULT, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing instructs this and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before any page exists.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with each wine's own bottle bound and the lines the shop cannot sell excluded by record range, then render the press file and 300 ppi proofs from that document.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever is asked for, so the route is chosen deliberately. Excluding a line is a commercial decision that has to be disclosed rather than performed quietly.
trajectory.produces: The press talker file at A6, 300 ppi proofs, and a record of which lines were excluded and why.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered card at true trim against the list, field by field and bottle by bottle, rather than at proof scale.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the output rather than the log. A field that never became a placeholder, a note that ends early and a bottle in the wrong card all look like success at the API boundary and all look plausible on a screen-scale proof.
trajectory.produces: A card-by-card reconciliation of the rendered talkers against the list.

trajectory.action: Sample the rendered card's own ground at trim, and if the lifted bottles sit in a patch against it, return to imaging: re-measure the stock value off the rendered card, re-fill all fourteen isolations onto that measured ground rather than the nominal swatch, re-judge the edge treatment across the whole set, then hand the re-grounded masters back to the merge to re-bind, re-merge and re-render.
trajectory.judgement: The ground was committed at step 8 against the only reference available then, the palette swatch and the flat PDF on screen, but the stock as it actually renders is a property of the converted document and cannot be read until a card exists at step 15. Matching the nominal Chalk White in good faith is not the same as matching the card, so the fault only surfaces here, after the merge, and the fix lives back on the imaging surface, which makes this a genuine InDesign to imaging loop rather than a re-run of the merge.
trajectory.produces: Fourteen bottles re-grounded to the measured stock, re-bound and re-merged, with the patch confirmed gone on every rendered card at trim.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for one cellar or hillside frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, grade it toward the house neutral and judge it beside the bottles. Then build the approval board within the placement cap and re-send only the entries reported as failed.
trajectory.judgement: An atmosphere frame at this band has to be quiet and plausible rather than a saturated sunset vineyard, which reads as the supermarket aisle no matter how good it looks at thumbnail size.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale frame, graded and judged in or out, and a persistent approval board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read restrained rather than either loud or fashionable. Numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one bad name kills the entire kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry or designer and the actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with roots at three canvas sizes (A1 bay panel at true physical dimensions, A4 bench list, tasting slides), the by-the-glass list as a real table, the recovered mark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left anchored wrapper, every photograph base64 inlined, family and weight declared on every text element, each root declaring its own canvas size. Upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check, export, then verify the first canvas through its rendition and the remaining canvases through the returned markup. Finally write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview shows the first canvas only. The design decisions, how much of the A1 is wine and how much is atmosphere, whether the bench list leads with the glass price or the grower, are the actual work, and the note has to let the next freelancer rebuild the talker from the same PDF without repeating the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document at three canvas sizes, its durable source HTML, a per-canvas markup audit, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the lift actually followed the bottle. Six wines are in near-black Burgundy and Rhone glass photographed on dark oak, so along the shoulder and around the capsule the bottle and the counter carry almost the same luminance, and the knockout returns a clean, feathered, entirely plausible cutout whose shoulder has been cut flat and whose capsule drags a soft halo of counter with it. On the dark original that edge is invisible. Which frames behave that way is a property of these particular bottles under this particular lamp and cannot be read off the list, the frame previews or the glass colour alone, because two equally dark bottles separated well and four did not.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care alone does not either, because the tool reports success either way and the artefact it returns looks like a competent cutout until it is placed on the pale card ground and looked at. Nothing states it: the brief says dark glass on a dark counter as a description of the shooting conditions and asks for bottles lifted onto a clean pale ground, which is an ordinary client requirement, and no asset description names which six wines are at risk. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to abandon the one-call route for those frames and lift them instead by selecting the bottle's own material, inverting and filling to the ground, which is a different operation with a different failure mode of its own.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-lift the affected bottles through a material-named selection, inverted and filled to the chosen ground, checking each result on the pale ground rather than on the original. Then re-judge the whole set together, because bottles lifted by two different routes carry different edge softness and will not sit as one shelf unless the edge treatment is re-decided across all fourteen, which in practice means re-lifting some of the eight that first succeeded.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen shelf cards in a bay where six of the most expensive bottles have a flattened shoulder and a grey halo, printed and stood in front of the actual bottles, in a shop whose whole proposition is that the card and the wine agree.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually exposes, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two things arrive only by running. First the granularity: the entire card body came out of the merchant's old system as one continuous tab-delimited story, so there are no per-field frames to map and everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story. Second the yield: the mapping readout of that story omits the run holding the stockist code while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed, every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns valid on internally consistent wrong arithmetic, the placeholder step reports complete success, and the two fields sitting past the omission never become placeholders at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before conversion and has no read-ahead, so the only route to it is to convert, export and read. The yield failure is worse, because it is produced by a convenience readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every tool downstream agrees with it. Nothing states it, since the brief says only to keep the card as it is and put this autumn's wines through it, and it is not a propagation re-run because the source of truth behind the mapping changes from a tool readout to a reconstructed story and the mapping is re-authored against it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the IDML content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order any rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping IDML and grepping for every placeholder before a single card is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen shelf cards that bind the wine, the grower and most of the block correctly while the score and the price are silently absent from every card, printed and stood on a shelf where the price is the one field the customer is looking for, with every tool in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every buyer's note actually reaches the card. The note frame in the printer's card is a fixed measure sized to last season's shorter copy, and this autumn's notes run from 90 to 340 characters because two hands wrote them. A frame like that does not spill and does not warn: the text that does not fit simply stops rendering, so an over-long note ends mid sentence at trim and the card still looks like a finished card. Which notes are affected depends on the merged output at true trim in the printer's own type at the printer's own measure, and cannot be worked out from character counts, because the field carries a mix of wide and narrow characters and the frame's real capacity is a property of the converted document rather than of the data.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because nothing in the merge or the render reports an overset condition and both return success, and the truncated card is visually indistinguishable from a card whose note was simply short. Nothing states it: the brief says the notes are ours and the acceptance bar says nothing may be shortened or reworded, which is the merchant's standing requirement rather than a warning, and no earlier step measures a frame or claims to have fitted anything. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is an escalation decision plus a change of what is bound rather than a re-run of the same binding.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify every truncated card by reading the rendered pages at true trim against the source note, not by counting characters. Then decide and disclose: the frame cannot be enlarged through this route and the merchant has forbidden rewriting, so the affected notes are escalated in writing before the file goes to the printer, with the shortest honest option offered (the merchant supplies a cut) and the cards re-merged and re-rendered once he answers.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A shelf of cards in which the four wines carrying the owner's own tasting notes, including the two he most wants people to try, break off mid sentence at the bottom of the frame, printed, cut and stood on the shelf for a customer base that reads the card the way it reads a review.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the ground every bottle was lifted onto actually agrees with the card it lands on, once the card is a rendered artefact rather than a swatch. The pale ground was chosen and committed at steps 8 and 9 against the only reference available then, the palette's Chalk White #F1ECE1 and the flat press PDF on screen, and the fourteen bottles were lifted onto a flat fill of that value. But the printer's card ground is a placed warm laid stock, not a flat process fill, and once the 2025 talker is converted at step 12 and a card is rendered at 300 ppi at trim at step 15, that ground reproduces a measurable step warmer and slightly darker than a flat #F1ECE1 fill. A rectangular cutout carrying a flat, cooler, swatch-matched ground, dropped into the card's graphic frame, then reads as a cool flat patch floating on a warmer card, on every one of the fourteen cards. On the cutout in isolation, and on any screen check against the swatch, the ground looks exactly right; the mismatch exists only where the two grounds meet on the rendered page.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the true stock value is a property of the converted and rendered document and does not exist until the PDF is converted and a card is rendered, which is strictly after the ground was committed and the bottles were lifted. Care cannot dodge it either: an agent that follows the ground decision gate in good faith and matches the cutout ground to the printer's own nominal Chalk White swatch produces cutouts that are numerically correct against the swatch and still patch against the rendered stock, and every tool in the chain reports success. Nothing states it, because the brief says only to lift the bottles onto a clean pale ground and keep the card as it is, and both the palette and the printer's own layout name the ground Chalk White, which is the swatch, not the stock as it reproduces. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is not to re-run the same lift but to leave the merge surface entirely, return to imaging, re-measure the ground off the rendered card, and re-fill every isolation to that measured value before the masters are re-bound.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Sample the rendered card's actual ground at trim, return to Photoshop and re-fill the fourteen isolations onto the measured stock value rather than the nominal swatch, which is a return to the imaging surface after the merge has already run, then re-bind the re-grounded masters through the image map, re-merge and re-render, and re-read the cards at trim to confirm the patch is gone on all fourteen. Because bottles lifted by the two different routes, the one-call knockout and the material-named selection, carry different edge softness against the new ground, the edge treatment has to be re-judged across the whole set once more, so in practice several of the eight that first succeeded are lifted again as well as re-grounded.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen shelf cards, printed and stood in the wooden fins in front of the actual bottles, on each of which the bottle sits inside a faint cool rectangle a shade off the card around it, the one flaw a label-reading customer at a 14 to 220 pound band reads instantly as cheap, in a shop whose whole proposition is that the card and the wine agree.

deliverables.name: Cellar & Cru autumn selection photography, fourteen wines at one shelf white
deliverables.spec: Sixteen supplied frames reconciled to fourteen wines and brought to one shelf white and one black point across two shooting evenings, with labels, capsules and glass colour honest to the bottle, delivered as one whole-bottle picture per wine at a settled bottle scale, plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log, one line per frame on why it differs from its neighbours, and every crop's reported detection and tradeoff metadata transcribed.

deliverables.name: Card-ready bottle cutouts on the agreed ground
deliverables.spec: Fourteen bottles lifted onto the single agreed pale ground for the printed card, with the cut edge following the glass along the shoulder and around the capsule and no counter carried in as halo, and the lift route recorded per wine because near-black glass on dark oak and a pale flute on the same counter cannot be produced the same way. Judged on the pale ground at card scale rather than on the dark original.

deliverables.name: The Cellar & Cru mark, recovered as placeable artwork
deliverables.spec: The merchant's monoline vine-and-key mark recovered from a photograph of a letterpressed card and delivered as placeable vector with the enclosed counter genuinely open, no opaque backing box, a real viewBox so it scales, and a high-resolution raster plate of the same artwork for the printed card. Delivered with a note on how it was derived and on the size below which the recovered artwork stops holding, so the shop can use the same mark on the next thing it prints.

deliverables.name: Autumn shelf-talker run, press file plus proofs
deliverables.spec: A6 portrait, one wine per page in list order, page count equal to the sellable wine count with the allocation-only lines excluded by record range, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every card binds grower, region, vintage, style, buyer's note, score, score source and price verbatim from the till export, plus that wine's own bottle in the card's graphic frame. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, which is handed back with the record of how it was derived so next season is a data change rather than a re-commission.

deliverables.name: Bay panel, bench list and November tasting slides
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document holding roots at three canvas sizes: an A1 shelf-end bay panel at true physical dimensions, an A4 by-the-glass bench list, and the trade-tasting slides. Live editable text throughout in one licensed type system, the by-the-glass list as a genuine table, the recovered mark as real vector artwork, every photograph carried as embedded image data. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, so prices can move without a re-commission and the design survives the document's own retention.

deliverables.name: Handover note and approval board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per frame what was applied and why it differs from its neighbours, the lift route per bottle, how the mark was recovered and where it stops holding, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the explicit statement that the card's typography remains the printer's because no font can reach that surface, what the conversion exposed and the mapping decisions taken against it, every list row questioned and its resolution, every note that will not fit the card as it stands, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent approval board carrying the graded selection and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The press talker file has exactly one page per sellable wine in list order and renders at 300 ppi at A6 trim, with no page for an allocation-only line.
verifiers_auto.how: Count pages in the rendered file against the reconciled sellable count, check the render call's resolution and the output raster dimensions, and read the wine name off every page against the excluded rows.

verifiers_auto.text: Every field the 2025 card carried, including score and price, appears on every merged page and matches its list row verbatim.
verifiers_auto.how: Round-trip the prepared template to IDML and grep for every expected placeholder, then read text off each rendered page and compare against its source row character for character.

verifiers_auto.text: No buyer's note is truncated on any rendered card, or every truncated note is named in the handover as escalated with the merchant's answer recorded.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare the note text visible on each rendered page at true trim against the full string in the list, and check the handover for the escalation of any that do not fit.

verifiers_auto.text: Each card carries the bottle of the wine named on that card.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the wine name off each rendered page and compare with the bottle image bound to it, never with the row's position in the returned list.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file exceeds its source frame on either axis and no crop or resize response carried an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare delivered dimensions against source dimensions and inspect every tradeoffs array in the imaging responses.

verifiers_auto.text: The exported Express document holds three canvases at three distinct declared sizes with the bay panel at true A1 physical dimensions, every photograph resolved to real image data rather than the importer's placeholder, the mark present as path shapes, and the by-the-glass list present as real table cells.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and per-slide dimensions from the export response and parse each canvas's returned markup for placeholder images, path-type shapes, table cell structure and resolved positions running past the declared canvas width.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported document carries a resolved licensed face and the intended numeric weight rather than a silent fallback.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare the resolved font families and weights in the returned markup against the kit's families and the numeric weights read from the style inventory.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered bottle sits in a ground patch on the rendered card: the card ground sampled just inside the edge of each bound bottle picture matches the card's own field ground rather than a flat swatch fill a step off it.
verifiers_auto.how: On each rendered page at trim, sample the ground inside the bottle's picture area near its edge and sample the card's field ground outside it, and assert the two values agree within tolerance rather than showing a rectangular step in hue and value.

verifiers_human.text: Laid out as the bay, the fourteen wines read as one selection shot on one evening at one bottle scale.
verifiers_human.how: View the fourteen whole-bottle pictures together and judge white point, black point and subject scale as a set rather than one at a time.

verifiers_human.text: Every label reads as the label the customer will recognise, with no bleached print, brassy capsule or crushed glass.
verifiers_human.how: Compare each delivered bottle against its source frame at label scale and against the other thirteen.

verifiers_human.text: On the pale card ground, every cut edge follows the bottle: no flattened shoulder, no clipped capsule, no halo.
verifiers_human.how: Place each cutout on the delivered ground and on a contrasting ground and inspect the shoulder and capsule at card reproduction size.

verifiers_human.text: The recovered mark still reads as the mark at the size it is printed on the card, not only at inspection size.
verifiers_human.how: View the mark at its actual reproduction width on the printed card and check the enclosed counter and the hairline rule are still open and present.

verifiers_human.text: The collateral reads restrained and grower-led, appropriate to a 14 to 220 pound bottle and a label-reading customer, rather than supermarket loud or fashion sparse.
verifiers_human.how: Review the cards, the bay panel, the bench list and the slides against the price band and audience description and reject shouting price treatments, saturated bottle photography and layouts that bury region or vintage.

verifiers_human.text: The handover escalates rather than conceals, naming the excluded lines, the notes that will not fit, and the fact that the card's typography could not be changed.
verifiers_human.how: Read the handover against the triage, conversion and render findings and check each is disclosed with the decision taken.

verifiers_human.text: On the rendered card each bottle sits on the card ground with no rectangular patch or halo of a different white around the picture, and the re-ground loop, if it was needed, is disclosed in the handover.
verifiers_human.how: View each rendered card at trim, look at the boundary of the bottle picture against the card ground for a cool flat rectangle or a step in value, and check the handover for the measured stock value and the fact that the cutouts were re-grounded to it.

decision_gates: The surface split: talkers to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is record per page, bay set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Which evening sets the shelf white, knowing a warm reference makes every white wine look oxidised across the whole bay.
How far to correct the warm evening before the correction itself becomes a glass or capsule colour the bottle is not.

Which pale ground the bottles are lifted onto, decided against the printer's card stock rather than against the screen, because the wrong white shows as a patch on all fourteen cards and forces every bottle to be lifted again.

Whether the bottle ground can be committed against the nominal Chalk White swatch at the isolation stage or must wait until a card has actually been rendered and the stock measured off it, since the press stock reproduces a step warmer than a flat #F1ECE1 fill and a swatch-matched cutout patches on all fourteen cards only once it is merged, forcing a return from the merge surface to imaging.
Lift route per bottle: the one-call knockout is right for a pale flute and wrong for near-black glass on dark oak, and the wrong route returns a plausible cutout that reports success.
Bottle scale across the set, decided as a bay rather than per picture, and re-decided once any bottle is lifted a different way.
How to name the selection that recovers the mark: naming the card pulls the paper, naming the ink's own colour and medium pulls the mark.
Whether the traced mark is artwork or merely output, including the backing path that rides along and the size below which the hairline rule stops holding.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the printer's own card body or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.
How to honour 'nothing shortened or reworded' when a note does not fit the frame the printer built, given no way to change that frame.
Whether the allocation-only lines are the agent's call to exclude or the merchant's, and how that is disclosed before printing.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a label-reading customer, plus the disclosure that no chosen face can reach the printed card at all.
Whether the licensed frame reads as a quiet cellar or as a saturated marketing vineyard, which is the wrong register for this band.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and this folder into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of wine bottles. IDENTITY: these are fourteen specific wines whose labels the customer recognises before reading a word, and a generated bottle fabricates a label, which on a card that also carries a grower, a vintage and a score is a false claim about what is in the bottle. The merchant's mark is a specific letterpressed device that must come back as the same mark, not a redrawn one, because it is already on the shop's door. SPEC: the merchant needs one card per sellable wine at A6 and 300 ppi with every field bound verbatim from their own till export, allocation-only lines absent, each card carrying its own bottle, and no delivered file larger than its source. None of that can be produced or checked by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season's list is a data change, and a native document with live text, a real table and real vector artwork so prices can move with the exchange rate. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, did this lift follow the glass, is this note complete at trim, is this the bottle this card names. That is not a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), the surface count is five and honestly declared, and no Illustrator tool is claimed: image_vectorize is counted as Photoshop-family, and document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector are never called because they sit on a polling helper this host does not have. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified; one record per page is confirmed for PDF output so page count equals row count is an exact gate; recordRange subsetting ('All', 'N', 'N-N') is verified and is how the allocation-only lines are excluded; outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is documented as silently ignored, so 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout on the merged .indd, using the N-N pageRange form because parameter interactions are brittle. Per-row image binding through an at-prefixed CSV column with bare filenames plus additionalImageFiles keyed to those filenames is verified visually. THE LOSSY-READOUT CHECKPOINT IS A DOCUMENTED LIVE FINDING: v3 records textContent dropping a 17-character run while keeping its line break, the validator returning VALID on the resulting offsets, prepare returning success, and only 3 of 5 mappings landing, with the IDML reconstruction landing 6 of 6. The one-story granularity is also a v3 finding (a continuous flow collapses to a single text frame), and this asset is specified as a tab-delimited continuous body plus a placed bottle image, which v3 observed yields text frames plus real graphic frames. The source PDF is specified as a real font-embedding press PDF because thin synthetic PDFs fail conversion opaquely. OVERSET: fixed-measure text simply not rendering is standard InDesign behaviour and the connector reports no overset condition anywhere, so the truncation is invisible in every response. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, colour temperature, single_color_saturation, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, remove_background with and without backgroundColor, fill_area and vectorize are all verified headless; the substrate-versus-ink prompt asymmetry, the enclosed-counter failure of remove_background, the collapse of disjoint lettering, the binary mask, the opaque path-0 rect and the missing viewBox are documented findings. THE STOCK-GROUND LOOP IS RENDER-VERIFIABLE: document_render_layout reproduces the press PDF's placed ground rather than a flat swatch, so sampling the merged card's ground against the cutout's flat fill detects the rectangular patch at trim, and the re-ground is a plain image_fill_area re-fill of each isolation to the measured value followed by a re-bind and re-merge, all headless, which is why this InDesign to imaging loop can only be found by rendering a card and never by any success message. No upscaling is asserted: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap signalled only in tradeoffs, so the bar scores the decision and the disclosure separately. EXPRESS: multi-root export with mixed canvas sizes is verified, mm canvases resolve at exactly 96 dpi so A1 and A4 are true physical canvases, tables survive as real tables with per-cell backgrounds and strokes, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, photographs must be base64 inlined because every external URL renders as an empty grey box, transport goes through the text/html upload because inlined photography passes the 70 KB inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows page one only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, embed chain is verified end to end and the task leans on the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript rule and the all-or-nothing kit call; the impossibility of getting a font file onto the InDesign surface is stated to the client rather than silently ignored. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, never the broken orientation filter, licensing returns genuine camera-scale files, board placements capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed claim, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files.
